limits: docker access on the host is root-equivalent: separation of service identities on one host, not host isolation
the broker trusts every allowed peer uid for every tenant (tenant authority: design path item 2)
holder strings are trusted within one service identity
a key already issued writes until the next CAS or its 1 h expiry (C12 a)
the operator directory is mounted into the app container for this test only

H6e, H6g: the default role-key mode (WP_BROKER unset) has no tenant isolation: the projector role key writes through any tenant's existing write alias (control C1 B_w) and updates another tenant's mapping (C14_reported d); reading another tenant is NOT claimed (C1 B_read records it: refused 403 at c6d3e85); alias add and re-point were REFUSED (403, control C4 and the fence CAS), so re-pointing is not demonstrated; only broker-minted keys are tenant- and epoch-scoped; a broker-mode deployment must not mint or place the role keys where the application runs
H6g C14c: a write without require_alias to an unused name of A's family, key still valid; the same writes after the CAS (key invalid, 401) are reported only (C14.c_after_cas_reported)
H6e C14d: whether a writer key can update its own tenant's mapping is observed, not assumed (see C14.d.own_mapping); tenant-local, reported, not judged
